key_insight: Local carbon intensity varies sharply across urban space and time, and a transferable surrogate model can estimate these variations accurately from limited municipal inputs.
engineering_relevance: This enables smarter control of buildings, EV charging, and district heating to cut emissions using high-resolution local carbon intensity estimates.
method: Compute spatially and temporally resolved carbon intensity factors at urban district scale.
Train surrogate models from limited inputs aligned with census grid cell information.
Compare decision-tree methods with a state-of-the-art neural network architecture for transferability and accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports carbon intensity values ranging from 0 to 316 g/kWh in a single city at summer noon, with case-study emission estimation errors up to 9% when local variation is ignored.
watch_item: Model accuracy and transferability may degrade in less dense or data-sparse regions, so deployment should validate local conditions before operational use.
paper_title: Quantification and Surrogate Model Estimation of Spatial-Temporal Carbon Intensity Factors
